system_note: What was billed: Position 1 billed as S36.020A (Contusion of spleen). The claim omitted J18.1 (lobar pneumonia) and includes R57.01 (cardiogenic shock). What the medical record documents: the treating physician (CDI query response) designated J18.1 (lobar pneumonia) as the PRINCIPAL diagnosis and stated the pneumonia "drove the septic cascade" (Principal Diagnosis Clarification, Clinical Documentation Improvement Queries, pp.158-240). The admission H&P and imaging document Grade IV splenic laceration with hemorrhagic (traumatic) shock and the need for emergent splenectomy and IR embolization (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, pp.242-475; Diagnostic Imaging Report - CT Trauma Panscan, p.117). The Discharge/Transfer Summary documents ventilator-associated pneumonia due to MSSA and notes extubation on ICU day 9 and transfer to an acute inpatient rehabilitation facility (Discharge / Transfer Summary, pp.859-860). Nephrology specifically documents rhabdomyolysis-associated AKI with peak CK 12,400 and creatinine 2.4 and states "Adequate urine output with aggressive hydration; no RRT indication" (Nephrology Consultation, Chart Notes, p.137). Why this is a Finding: (1) Principal-sequencing - CDI/physician attestation names J18.1 (lobar pneumonia) as the principal diagnosis and instructs septic shock/ARDS be coded as secondary; the claim instead lists a splenic contusion (S36.020A) in principal position. The physician-selected principal diagnosis is authoritative for sequencing (Principal Diagnosis Clarification, Clinical Documentation Improvement Queries, pp.158-240). (2) Missing principal diagnosis - J18.1 is documented in the Problem List and the CDI clarification as principal but is not present in the billed diagnosis position 1. (3) Unsupported/incorrect diagnosis - R57.01 (cardiogenic shock) is billed but the contemporaneous H&P documents hemorrhagic/traumatic shock from splenic hemorrhage (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, pp.242-475) and the record contains no documentation supporting a cardiogenic etiology (no diagnostic data supporting cardiogenic shock; troponin noted negative in H&P labs). The record does document traumatic/hemorrhagic shock (T79.4XXA) and septic shock as in-hospital complications. Recommended correction: re-sequence the claim so principal diagnosis = J18.1 (lobar pneumonia), remove R57.01 (cardiogenic shock) or replace it with the documented shock etiology (traumatic/hemorrhagic or septic shock) supported by notes, and revise the splenic diagnosis coding to reflect the documented Grade IV splenic laceration (documentation: H&P and CT Panscan) rather than a contusion. All listed procedures (intubation, splenectomy, IR embolization, chest tube, pelvic external fixation, femur IM nailing, transfusion, central infusion device, >96-hour ventilation) are supported by the record and may remain. Evidence (document/section/pages cited) used in this determination is provided below.
rationale_letter: Re: Audit determination - MR_28 Dear Provider/Coding Team, We have completed our DRG-level review of the above inpatient admission. After review of the medical record and the clinical documentation improvement (CDI) physician clarification, we have determined that the claim requires coding correction(s). This determination is based on physician attestation and contemporaneous chart documentation as described below. Finding: Principal diagnosis sequencing error and unsupported diagnosis (cardiogenic shock). Basis for Finding: - The CDI query response (Principal Diagnosis Clarification) documents that the treating physician selected J18.1 (lobar pneumonia) as the PRINCIPAL diagnosis and explicitly states: "The pneumonia (J18.1 - lobar pneumonia confirmed on imaging) drove the septic cascade. Septic shock and ARDS are complications of the pneumonia and should be coded as secondary diagnoses." (Principal Diagnosis Clarification, Clinical Documentation Improvement Queries, pp.158-240). This attestation mandates sequencing J18.1 as the principal diagnosis. - The admission History & Physical and CT trauma panscan document severe polytrauma including Grade IV splenic laceration requiring emergent splenectomy and pelvic hemorrhage requiring IR embolization (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, pp.242-475; Diagnostic Imaging Report - CT Trauma Panscan, p.117). These support the procedures billed (splenectomy, IR embolization, external fixation, IM nailing, thoracostomy, transfusion, prolonged mechanical ventilation). - The record does not contain clinical documentation supporting cardiogenic shock (R57.01). The H&P documents hemorrhagic/traumatic shock from splenic hemorrhage and later septic physiology - not a primary cardiogenic etiology (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, pp.242-475). Nephrology documents AKI secondary to rhabdomyolysis and states no RRT was indicated (Nephrology Consultation, Chart Notes, p.137), which further supports the clinical course without a cardiogenic shock diagnosis. Corrections to be made: 1. Re-sequence the claim so that the principal diagnosis is J18.1 (lobar pneumonia), POA as documented. The CDI physician explicitly designated J18.1 as the principal diagnosis (Principal Diagnosis Clarification, pp.158-240). 2. Remove R57.01 (cardiogenic shock) from the coded list unless the provider supplies contemporaneous documentation supporting a cardiogenic etiology. The chart documents hemorrhagic/traumatic shock (T79.4XXA) and later septic physiology; code accordingly. 3. Revise the splenic diagnosis code to reflect the documented Grade IV splenic laceration (per CT Panscan and H&P) rather than a splenic contusion, and ensure POA/operative link to the splenectomy (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, pp.242-475; Diagnostic Imaging Report - CT Trauma Panscan, p.117). 4. The documented procedures (endotracheal intubation, splenectomy, insertion of pleural device/chest tube, IR embolization/occlusion of internal iliac branch, pelvic external fixation, femur IM nailing, transfusion, central infusion device, and >96-hour mechanical ventilation) are supported and may remain coded; please ensure any device insertion codes correspond to the specific procedural notes. If you disagree with the physician-designated principal diagnosis (J18.1) or believe R57.01 is supported, please provide the contemporaneous documentation that supports alternative sequencing or the cardiogenic shock etiology so we may reconsider the claim. Absent such documentation, we will proceed with the corrections above. Sincerely, Clinical Claims Audit Team

evidence_cited.excerpt: Impression Multi-system trauma with hemodynamically significant splenic and pelvic hemorrhage requiring immediate intervention.
Rhabdomyolysis-associated AKI with CK peak 12,400 and creatinine 2.4. Adequate urine output with aggressive hydration; no RRT indication.
Extubation was successful on ICU day 9 with brief VAP requiring aggressive pulmonary toileting rather than reintubation.
The patient is transferred to an acute inpatient rehabilitation facility for continued orthopedic and functional recovery with non-weight-bearing precautions on the right lower extremity.
